newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia deficit may hit C$400 mln -report.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia deficit may hit C$400 mln -report.

text.p: British Columbia's government will record a deficit of C$300 million to C$400 million in the 1996/97 fiscal year despite plans to cut C$750 million in spending, the Globe and Mail newspaper reported on Monday.
Quoting an unidentified government source, the newspaper said the province's latest plans do not anticipate a balanced budget until 1997/98.

Premier Glen Clark's government had projected a surplus of C$87 million in the current fiscal year ending March 1997. But it has recently said that that forecast has been thrown awry because of slower than expected growth.
The government has announced plans to cut 3,500 jobs and transfer C$400 million from a fund set up to revitalize the forest industry into its general revenues.
Opposition politicians accuse the government of covering up the deterioration in the province's finances until after a May election in which the New Democratic Party narrowly held on to power.
Government officials were not immediately available to comment on the Globe report.
